raw_response:
## My thinking this season

I've been farming this same 6 mu for thirty years now, so I know these fields well. Soil is decent loam, nothing special but responds well if you treat it right. With my senior high background I pay attention to what the extension station says, but honestly after three decades I mostly trust what I've seen work on my own ground.

**Wheat first.** Last year I got about 470 kg/mu — not bad for our area, but I think I can push to 480-500 this year if the spring rains come at the right time. I'll sow in the second week of October like always, using Jimai 22 — it's been reliable, good lodging resistance, and my neighbor Old Wang got 520 kg/mu with it last season. I save some seed but mostly buy fresh every 2-3 years so the variety stays pure.

For fertilizer, I'll do about 16 kg N/mu total, split 60/40 — base application of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before sowing, then topdress urea at jointing around early April. Phosphorus and potash come with the compound, roughly 7-8 kg each. The compound is expensive but it's easier than mixing myself, and for 6 mu it's manageable. I'll irrigate before sowing (the soil is dry now), then at jointing, heading, and grain filling if needed — usually 3 times, sometimes 4 if the spring is dry. Well water isn't cheap with electricity and the metering now, but wheat without irrigation here is a gamble I won't take.

**Then maize right after wheat harvest in mid-June.** This is the tight part — I have maybe 3-4 days between combining the wheat and getting maize in the ground. I do no-till direct seeding with a hired planter (about 30 yuan/mu) — saves time and the wheat residue helps hold moisture. Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605, whichever the seed shop has; both are solid. 

Maize I'll target about 550 kg/mu. N rate around 14-15 kg/mu, mostly as one topdressing at V6-V8 stage (the big-flare stage) because putting urea down at planting in our heat just volatilizes away. If July is dry I'll irrigate once at tasseling — critical stage, can't skip. Usually only need 1-2 irrigations because summer rains cover the rest.

**Pesticides:** herbicide for both crops is standard — 2,4-D plus tribenuron on wheat in spring, atrazine-based mix on maize pre-emergence. I scout for aphids on wheat in May and corn borer on maize in July; only spray if I actually see them, no point spraying on schedule.

**Labor:** My wife helps with scouting and some hand work, my son is in town working so he only comes back for harvest weekends. Most heavy work — plowing, combining, planting — I hire out. For 6 mu the machinery cost is worth it; I'm 60, my back isn't what it was.

**Budget check:** roughly 450 yuan/mu on wheat inputs and 350 yuan/mu on maize, so about 4,800 yuan total for the year. That's within what I can cover from last year's grain sales plus the small grain subsidy. No borrowing needed, which is how I like it.
